Description: 3-phase BLDC gimbal motor with integrated AS5048A encoder. 12 V, 11 pole pairs, 6.34 ohm phase-to-phase, 1.08 mH, Kt = 0.08 Nm/A, 1.1 A nominal / 1.9 A stall, 40x20 mm. Encoder factory-aligned to rotor; phase leads terminate in unmarked bare surface pads.

14-bit on-axis magnetic rotary encoder. Integrated on M1, not sold separately. Supports SPI and PWM, but only the PWM output is broken out on this unit — approximately 12 effective bits at ~1 kHz update rate.

3-phase BLDC driver board based on the Texas Instruments DRV8313. 8-30 V input, 2.5 A per phase, 3-PWM interface, onboard 3V3 LDO, 26x21 mm. No current sensing, so the drive runs in voltage-torque mode.
Dual-core 240 MHz microcontroller board with BLE and a CP2102 USB-C interface. Core 1 runs the FOC loop, core 0 runs the BLE HID stack.
Momentary SPST pushbutton, through-hole. GPIO 32 to GND with internal pull-up. Short press = play/pause, long press = mode toggle.
12 V DC barrel-jack power adapter, 1 A minimum. Powers the driver rail only; the ESP32 is USB-powered in this revision.
Jumper wire assortment, male-male and male-female.
Hookup wire, 22 AWG stranded. Soldered directly to the motor phase pads.

1 ohm current shunt resistor, 2 W or better. Placed in series with one phase for the current/torque capture; measured differentially, since neither terminal sits at ground. Not part of the running build.
2-channel USB oscilloscope, 100 MS/s. Used for the phase PWM captures. Listed for reproducibility only.
